newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Minor Metals - China cobalt price seen steady.
newsitem.headline: Minor Metals - China cobalt price seen steady.

text.p: Chinese cobalt prices are holding steady even as world prices continue to climb, Far East traders said on Tuesday.
Traders in Hong Kong and China quoted Chinese cobalt prices at between 380-420 yuan (US$45-50) a kg, or $20-25 a lb.
The blue metal was arriving in Hong Kong, mostly from Russia, at $22.90 per pound CIF for 99.5 percent ingots, a good $1 per pound higher than last week's quotes, traders said.
While traders in Europe had said the market was extremely tight, trading sources in Asia were not so sure. One said supply in China was adequate given slower usage at this time of year.
They said the Chinese market was difficult to gauge because it depended to some extent on the construction sector, which had been slowing since Beijing tightened credit in 1993.
Cobalt is used in the process of making steel, to tint paint and glass and in the production of batteries.
Speaking by telephone from the southern city of Guangzhou, a Chinese trader said if Beijing eased credit restrictions in 1997, this could lead to an upturn in cobalt demand.
But he and others agreed demand in China has remained static and this has manifested itself in steady domestic prices.
China needed 2,300 to 2,500 tonnes of cobalt a year, another Chinese trading source said.
Of that, 1,000 tonnes was produced domestically and 1,500 tonnes was imported, primarily from Russia, Canada and Zaire.

"When the construction industry is good, demand (for cobalt) is good," he said. "There is potential for demand to pick up to (a minimum of) 2,500 tonnes a year but this depends on the economic and financial outlook in China to support demand."
But he said many Chinese end-users still held stocks, which while small would keep them going through the traditionally slow period between Christmas and Chinese New Year in February.
A Western trader in Hong Kong said Chinese imports of and demand for cobalt were unclear because the industry was characterised by irregularities.

"It's historically jumpy," he said. "There are imports outside regular channels, imports for the central stockpile, imports for trading that are then re-exported, duty dodging and duty discounting, so it's hard to know what is really going on."
"But there hasn't been much movement in price because any buying has been on a hand-to-mouth basis and I expect that is where it will stay until after Chinese new year," he said.
Japanese cobalt traders and end-users said they were keenly watching the result of a tender by the U.S. Defense Logistic Agency (DLA) on Monday to sell cobalt rondelles and granules.

"The tender result will be made public within a few days, and that will determine if Japanese end-users will buy cobalt in the spot market by the end of this year," an official with a major trading house said.
The bottom line for Japanese end-users was to keep stocks as low as possible ahead of the New Year holidays, traders said.
"But some end-users are still showing buying interest," another industry official said.

In the spot market, high-grade cobalt was being quoted at around $23 a lb against about $22 a week earlier, traders said. Russian cobalt was being quoted at between $21 and $21.50 a lb this week, they said.

Zaire's state-owned metal giant Gecamines sent senior marketing officials to Japan last week in an attempt to figure out the metal demand there, traders said. But the details of their meetings with Japanese customers were not available.

Traders in Hong Kong and China dismissed the possible impact of increased copper and cobalt production in Zaire after Gecamines and Swiss-based Groupe Lundin on Sunday signed a joint venture agreement to mine vast resources of copper and cobalt at Tenke Fungurume in southern Shaba province. -- Lynne O'Donnell, Hong Kong newsroom (852) 2843-6470; Eiichiro Tokumoto, Tokyo newsroom (81) 3-3432-7391
